sources.title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, Act No. 37
NDP Act General Application and Implementation Directive, 20 March 2025

citation.title: Review the applicable lawful basis and consent evidence.

entries.explanation: Consent requirements depend on the processing and its lawful basis.
entries.limit: Reserved for P3-09 at note severity; absence of a code pattern does not establish missing consent.

entries.explanation: An identifiable person's account information warrants proportionate safeguards.
entries.limit: A valid account-number check digit neither identifies a person nor proves unlawful processing.

citation.title: Review protection of bank verification identifiers.

entries.explanation: Identification numbers linked to individuals require appropriate protection.
entries.limit: Eleven digits alone do not establish a BVN, sensitive biometric data or a legal breach.

citation.title: Review protection of identifying email addresses.

entries.explanation: An email address may identify an individual and need protection.
entries.limit: A role mailbox, example address or public contact is not automatically an unlawful disclosure.

citation.title: Review personal-data exposure in response models.

entries.explanation: Response fields warrant review for necessity and authorised disclosure.
entries.limit: A model declaration alone cannot prove that a field is returned or lacks authorisation.

citation.title: Review personal identifiers stored in configuration.

entries.explanation: Configuration can expose identifiers beyond their intended processing purpose.
entries.limit: A configuration value may be synthetic; finding it does not prove an actual disclosure.

citation.title: Review personal identifiers in fixtures and seed data.

entries.explanation: Test data warrants checks for unnecessary use of personal identifiers.
entries.limit: A plausible identifier is not proof that a fixture contains real personal data.

citation.title: Review personal identifiers exposed to logging.

entries.explanation: Logging can extend access and retention beyond the original purpose.
entries.limit: A source pattern does not establish deployed logging, retention duration or a legal breach.

entries.explanation: Database design warrants proportionate security and encryption review.
entries.limit: A migration alone cannot establish encryption at rest; section 39 does not mandate blanket column encryption.

citation.title: Review the context of a possible personal identifier.

entries.explanation: Context determines whether an eleven-digit value relates to an individual.
entries.limit: Keep at note severity; the value may be neither a BVN nor a NIN.

citation.title: Review protection of national identity identifiers.

entries.explanation: Identification numbers linked to individuals require appropriate protection.
entries.limit: A labelled value is a detection signal, not verification of an issued NIN or proof of a breach.

citation.title: Review protection of identifying telephone numbers.

entries.explanation: A telephone number may identify an individual and need protection.
entries.limit: A recognised prefix does not prove a number is assigned or that processing is unlawful.

citation.title: Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis.

entries.explanation: Processor engagements and international transfers warrant documented safeguards and an applicable basis.
entries.limit: A package, hostname or region setting does not establish a transfer, recipient role, adequacy or unlawfulness.
